newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador coffee crop 3.06 mln bag - Procafe.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador coffee crop 3.06 mln bag - Procafe.

text.p: El Salvador's coffee crop is seen ending the 1996-1997 cycle producing around 3.06 million 46-kilo bags, the Salvadoran Foundation for Coffee Investigation (Procafe) said Thursday.

The forecast, little different from the one given by the Salvadoran Coffee Council, has the crop still coming in around the 3.0 million 46-kilo bags mark which it has roughly averaged in recent years.

Procafe's forecast includes a five percent loss of beans from earlier expectations due to rain damage at the start of the year. It is based on a sample survey in the different coffee growing zones of the country which has a total of 16,191 plantations.

Procafe spokeswoman Sandra Caceres told Reuters that bean harvesting started normally in mid-October and that cherries are in a normal maturing stage. She said few problems of leaf rot had been detected this cycle.
A statement from Procafe recommended growers to speed up harvesting in low and medium altitude levels where cherries are ripe because of the recent rains that have passed over growing areas.
